cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Find the Real Authority
cards.instruction: Probe until you know who can approve, block, or reverse the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll coordinate the trip booking. Before I commit us, who could still stop it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The committee approved it. Please book before we lose the coach.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll keep the booking moving. Just tell me whose objection could stop the deposit; you can give me the short version.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The treasurer's, but she's away. Her deputy has the bank login.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, we'll use your route. Can the deputy release the money alone, or does she need the treasurer's say-so? You make the introduction however suits you; I'll take the call from there.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims booking coordination; A3 shortens the request to respect B urgency and A5 grants introduction method while probing whether deputy access carries actual release power.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 approval/deadline causes A3 residual deposit veto question; B4 treasurer/login split causes A5 independent-permission question.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants transport secured and B4 offers a practical route; A promises to take the follow-up rather than burden B with the whole process.

heightening.evidence: A5 distinguishes a person who can log in from one who can authorize the outcome.

specificity.evidence: A1 trip, B2 coach and B4 deposit authority make the distinction concrete.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 say-so versus login is economical in concept, though the final introduction offer adds length.
